newsitem.title: UK: Oftel proposes to reduce Mercury regulation.
newsitem.headline: Oftel proposes to reduce Mercury regulation.

text.p: British telecoms regulator OFTEL said on Wednesday it was proposing to reduce the regulatory demands imposed on Mercury in the early 1980s.

Oftel said Mercury would have a simplified licence covering both domestic and international operations and that a number of prescriptive obligations would be removed to reflect Mercury's non-dominant position, particularly in the domestic market.

Oftel also said that rapidly developing competition in the international market may allow it to withdraw further still from detailed regulation and it would be keeping the proposals under review, with a view to lifting them in whole or in part as soon as competition is sufficient to allow it to do so.

The proposals include replacing Mercury's existing service obligation for inland services by the standard obligation applied to all operators having a newer, slimline licence. International service obligations will remain unchanged.
Oftel is also backing new conditions to ensure fair trading and effective competition in international markets.

In addition, it is proposing to replace Cable and Wireless subsdiary Mercury's obligation to publish its prices with a more flexible condition modelled on the price publication requirements in the draft International Facilities Licence, on which the Department of Trade and Industry is currently holding consultations.

Analysts said the Oftel move was expected and would probably not lead to substantially more customers: "They can price services for different customers, but it is not a big deal," said James Golob at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
